wu: Toy Charades: Students take turns miming a toy (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) while classmates guess, saying 'Is it a...?' The mimer responds 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn't!'
wuAlt: Toy Memory Game: Students match picture cards of toys, saying 'I have got a...' when they find a pair
Toy Toss: Students toss a soft ball and name a toy before catching it, saying 'I like the...'
pres: Show flashcards of two toys (e.g., big ball, small ball) and model 'The ball is bigger than the ball.' Use real toys (teddy and car) to demonstrate 'The teddy is smaller than the car.' Ask students to repeat and point to the bigger/smaller toy.
presAlt: Toy Comparison Story: Draw a simple story of a boy with a big teddy and a girl with a small doll, narrating 'The teddy is bigger than the doll.'
Toy Sorting Line: Students line up toy flashcards from smallest to biggest, saying 'The car is smaller than the ball.'
prac: Toy Comparison Worksheet: Students look at picture pairs (e.g., big puzzle, small puzzle) and write 'The puzzle is bigger than the puzzle.' in pairs, with teacher monitoring for accuracy.
pracAlt: Toy Comparison Board Game: Students roll a dice and move, landing on a toy to compare with the teacher's example, saying 'The car is bigger than the teddy.'
Toy Comparison Chain: Students sit in a circle and each adds a toy comparison, e.g., 'The ball is bigger than the doll. The doll is smaller than the car.'
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes toy comparisons (e.g., 'Draw a big ball and a small car. The ball is bigger than the car.') and students draw, then compare with a partner.
re: Toy Relay Race: Teams race to grab two toys from a box, run back, and say 'The [toy] is bigger than the [toy]!' before tagging the next player.
prod: Toy Shop Roleplay: Students work in pairs, one as shopkeeper, one as customer. Customer asks 'Can I have the [toy], please?' and shopkeeper responds 'Here you are. It's bigger than the [other toy].'
rw: Read and Match: Students read short sentences like 'The doll is smaller than the car.' and match them to picture pairs on a worksheet, then write one similar sentence.
st: Goodbye Song: Sing 'The Wheels on the Bus' with toy-themed lyrics ('The teddy on the bus goes hug and hug, hug and hug...'), followed by sticker chart rewards and a high-five line.
g: Students mark pictures of toys on their bingo card when the teacher calls out 'Bigger than the ball!'
Students flip over toy cards to find matching pairs, saying 'I have got a...' when they find one
Students toss a ball and name a toy bigger/smaller than the one they catch, saying 'The car is bigger than the teddy!'
Teams race to line up toy flashcards from smallest to biggest, saying 'The puzzle is smaller than the ball!'
Students take turns being shopkeeper and customer, asking 'Can I have the..., please?' and comparing toys
diff: Fast finishers: Draw their own toy comparison and write 3 sentences, e.g., 'My ball is bigger than my doll.'
Support: Use word banks with 'bigger', 'smaller', and toy names to help write sentences
hw: Find a toy worksheet in the library folder and complete it
Draw two toys at home and write 'The [toy] is bigger than the [toy].'
Ask family about their favorite toys and write one sentence comparing them
tip: Use real toys or colorful flashcards to make comparisons tangible—Moroccan learners respond well to hands-on activities with familiar objects.
